Gun violence will impact you, no matter where you live. Get involved on the local and state levels today.

For more than two centuries, the Supreme Court has affirmed that states have broad authority over the corporations they create.

States can use that power to cut off corporate and dark money in politics at every level.
ampr.gs/4clbhoU

Wednesday, April 15, join CAP and the Community Colleges Coalition to explore how community colleges are adapting to new federal and state policies. Together, we’ll highlight promising strategies, share insights from across the nation, and align advocacy priorities for the year ahead. ampr.gs/4stfcGi
Renters are facing unprecedented housing costs and fewer options. americanprogress.org/shareab…

Trump's war in Iran is padding the pockets of oil and gas CEOs. Meanwhile, Americans are seeing historically high prices at the pump. Catherine Wolfram explains:

Video

Simply by surviving the war and inflicting damage on U.S. partners, Iran has emerged stronger than it was before the war, while the United States achieved none of its objectives, suffered costly losses, and has weakened its strategic position vis-a-vis its adversaries. ampr.gs/4mptQgm

Prior to the ACA, health insurance companies discriminated against sick people by denying them coverage altogether. It's time to strengthen these protections and ban prior authorization. americanprogress.org/article…

Whether or not the ceasefire represents an enduring end to the war in Iran, the result of the six-week campaign is incontestable: The United States is in a weaker position than before the war. americanprogress.org/article…

#AANHPIEqualPay is about more than just fair wages. It also includes having workplaces free from discrimination and harassment, but we can't identify problems we don't measure.

The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) is considering rescinding the EEO-1 data collection that helps enforce gender and racial nondiscrimination in employment. Read more on ending workplace discrimination: ampr.gs/4cezopb
Health insurance companies have been price gouging employers and workers for too long. CAP has a plan to rein in outrageous costs and stop exploitation of patients: americanprogress.org/article…

While it is unclear whether the two-week ceasefire will lead to a lasting resolution to the war in Iran, much of the economic damage has already been done, with consumers and businesses forced to suffer the expensive consequences for months to come. ampr.gs/4cggL42

All eyes on Hawaii: The state is one step closer to getting corporate and dark money out of politics—and further than any other state has gone toward making Citizens United v. FEC irrelevant. Watch this space for updates.

Video
From WIC to the NIH to K-12 funding, Trump's proposed budget cuts would severely reduce federal assistance to ordinary Americans and sink money toward war. americanprogress.org/article…

The Ten Commandments live vibrantly in many Americans’ hearts, homes, and houses of worship. But taxpayer-funded classrooms must uphold education policies that value religious freedom for all students and families. americanprogress.org/article…
Trump's budget request would be a poor use of America’s national resources, making a clear statement that the Trump administration believes struggling Americans are on their own. ampr.gs/3Q6IjS4

The Trump administration is attempting to waive the Endangered Species Act under the guise of national security. Stripping away critical environmental safeguards isn't protecting America—it’s fast‑tracking the extinction of the Gulf’s only endemic whale while oil production is already at record highs. ampr.gs/41eqsuZ

Health care should be affordable, accessible, and work for the people—not just insurance companies or hospital systems. CAP's new proposal for a patients' bill of rights has solutions to immediately lower costs and strengthen patient protections.

Video

Rising health care costs are pushing Americans to a breaking point. 

CAP's new proposal for a patients' bill of rights would provide immediate relief on premiums, deductibles, and insurance denials: americanprogress.org/article…

CAP’s analysis of the Gun Violence Archives data shows that 17 of the 50 most populous American cities have seen a more than 50% decline in their gun victimization rate from 2021 to 2025. The historic progress being achieved in these cities can provide insights into how to deliver lasting public safety benefits. ampr.gs/3NPtfI1
